report.source_text: During the TEE, the following findings were reported: ejection fraction (EF) of 40–45%; very severe aortic aneurysm (AI); dilated aortic aneurysm measuring 6.9 cm; mild mitral regurgitation (MR); minimal tricuspid regurgitation (TR); mild pulmonary insufficiency (PI); pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) of 50 mm/Hg; severe left ventricle enlargement measuring 136 cm/m2 with mild systolic dysfunction; a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp (NCC) mostly resembling vegetation; very severe aortic regurgitation (AR), aneurysmal aortic root (annulus, 3.1 cm; sinus of valsalva (SOV), 4.2 cm; effacement of sinotubular junction (STJ)); aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta with the proximal portion measuring 6.8 cm and the distal portion measuring 3.9 cm; a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating about 1.3 cm after the aortic valve (AV); the dissecting flap appearing thickened and infected; and mild circumferential pericardial effusion (5 mm around all cardiac chambers).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old male presented with fever and chills. Initial lab tests showed elevated WBC, neutrophilia, lymphopenia, anemia, and markedly elevated ESR, while blood cultures were negative. A transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) revealed severe aortic aneurysm (6.9 cm), aortic dissection with an infected linear flap, a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass resembling vegetation on the noncoronary cusp, and very severe aortic regurgitation. Due to these critical findings, the patient underwent an emergent Bentall procedure, involving the replacement of the aortic valve, ascending aorta, and aortic root with a mechanical composite graft. Post-operatively, the patient was managed in the cardiac ICU, initiated on warfarin, and continued on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Discharge lab results showed improved WBC and stable hemoglobin.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with fever and chills, suggesting an infectious process.
Initial lab tests showed elevated WBC (11.1 x 10^3 UL), neutrophilia (80%), lymphopenia (17%), anemia (Hb 10 mg/dL), and markedly elevated ESR (107 mm/hour).

Transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) revealed a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass on the noncoronary cusp mostly resembling vegetation, very severe aortic aneurysm (6.9 cm), aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta, a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating 1.3 cm after the aortic valve, and the dissecting flap appearing thickened and infected.
The patient underwent an emergent Bentall procedure, replacing the aortic valve, ascending aorta, and root with a mechanical composite graft.
Post-operatively, the patient was admitted to the cardiac ICU, started on warfarin, and continued antibiotic therapy.
Discharge lab results showed improved WBC (4000 × 10^3 UL) and stable hemoglobin (9.10 mg/dL).
